features.name: validatePathWithinRoot + O_NOFOLLOW tmpdir symlink attack prevention
features.counter_case: Cortex's path handling is simpler today; adding full validation means every tool call pays a resolve/normalize cost, and Windows UNC paths may need special handling.
features.summary: Validates resolved path is within projectRoot; uses O_NOFOLLOW when writing tmpdir session marker to block symlink replacement on world-writable Linux /tmp.

features.name: CamelCase/snake_case compound identifier tokenizer + nameMatchBonus length-ratio scoring
features.counter_case: Cortex's KB is concept-level (entity names, not raw symbol names), so CamelCase splitting may produce false positives against entity description text.
features.summary: Splits 'getUserName' into tokens; preserves compound 'getusername' alongside parts; exact match=80, prefix match=10-40 scaled by length ratio, substring=10.

features.name: Bounded Damerau-Levenshtein edit distance + stem variant expansion
features.counter_case: Cortex plans fuse.js for fuzzy matching (Phase 0.9); adopting this instead means dropping fuse.js before it ships, creating churn.
features.summary: O(min(a,b)) memory bounded edit-distance (early-exit when > maxDist); stem expansion covers -ing/-tion/-ment/-ies/-es/-s/-ed/-er for FTS prefix queries.

features.name: Marker-delimited git hook sync (post-commit/merge/checkout, async background)
features.counter_case: Cortex's Phase 0.10 already has a detailed spec; adopting codegraph's implementation directly may conflict if Cortex's design includes extra checks (e.g., diff-size gating before sync).
features.summary: Installs post-commit/merge/checkout hooks delimited by MARKER_BEGIN/END markers; runs `cortex sync` async in background; honors core.hooksPath; idempotent and removable.

features.name: SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS in MCP initialize (tight playbook, not lobby prose)
features.counter_case: Cortex's tool descriptions contain workflow coaching because each tool needs to explain when to use it; moving to a centralized instructions block requires ensuring agents actually receive and honor the MCP initialize payload.
features.summary: Tool-selection-by-intent, common chains, anti-patterns, limitations — all in <50 lines. No 'INSTEAD of X' lobbying in individual tool descriptions.

features.name: Schema migration system with schema_versions table
features.counter_case: Cortex's storage is JSON files, not SQLite; migrations must be adapted to a schema-versioned JSON envelope rather than SQL DDL.
features.summary: Each migration has version, description, up(db). runMigrations() applies only pending (fromVersion). schema_versions table records applied migrations.

features.name: Field-qualified search query (kind:function path:src/api lang:python name:auth)
features.counter_case: Cortex's KB is concept-level text, not structured symbol nodes; kind: and lang: filters require Cortex to have typed entities, which it only partially does today.
features.summary: Tokenizer preserves quoted spans. Unknown field prefixes pass through to FTS. OR-composition within each filter type, AND across filter types.

features.name: SQLite WAL mode + bounded busy_timeout (≤30s) + stale-PID lock detection
features.counter_case: Cortex doesn't use SQLite yet; adopting WAL + busy_timeout requires the storage unification (Stage 4) to land first.
features.summary: WAL mode lets readers proceed during a writer; busy_timeout ≤30s (old default was 120s); FileLock checks PID liveness and auto-removes stale locks from dead processes.

features.name: Container node structural outline (class/struct → member signatures not full body)
features.counter_case: Cortex's `source` tool works on raw files, not structured AST nodes; implementing 'structural outline' requires AST extraction (Phase 0.13) to land first — this is a second-order dependency.
features.summary: CONTAINER_NODE_KINDS (class/struct/interface/trait/protocol/enum/namespace/module) triggers structural outline mode: member names + signatures + line numbers instead of full body.

features.name: Line numbers in explore output (cat -n style, A/B env override)
features.counter_case: Cortex's `source` already returns line-numbered output via Read tool convention; adding it to context packs adds a few percent token overhead for every snippet.
features.summary: numberSourceLines() prepends 1-based line numbers (matching Read tool convention). CODEGRAPH_EXPLORE_LINENUMS=0 disables for A/B measurement.

features.name: Path relevance scoring + test-file deprioritization (-15)
features.counter_case: Cortex's search is on entity names/descriptions, not file paths; path relevance scoring applies directly only if Cortex surfaces source file paths alongside results.
features.summary: fileName match +10, dir match +5, path match +3; test files penalized -15 unless query contains 'test'/'spec'. Uses base terms only (no stems, to avoid inflating path scores).

features.name: V8 turboshaft WASM Zone OOM fix + relaunch guard env var
features.counter_case: Cortex doesn't use tree-sitter today; this fix is only needed if/when Phase 0.13 (tree-sitter extractors) ships.
features.summary: `--liftoff-only` prevents V8 turboshaft from OOM-killing tree-sitter grammar compilation on Node 22/24. Self-relaunch via spawnSync with CODEGRAPH_WASM_RELAUNCHED guard.

features.name: isTestFile comprehensive multi-language detection
features.counter_case: Cortex works at entity level, not file level; test file detection is only useful if Cortex indexes file paths alongside entities.
features.summary: Covers Python (test_foo.py), Go (foo_test.go), Java/Kotlin CamelCase (FooTest.kt), directory patterns (__tests__/, spec/, jvmTest/). Also detects examples/fixtures/benchmarks as non-production.

features.name: Adaptive output budget (4 project-size tiers)
features.counter_case: Cortex's context packs are designed for a fixed budget; file-count-based tiers would need to be recomputed on every request and may not align with Cortex's token-budget-first design.
features.summary: Four tiers (<500, <5k, <15k, ≥15k files). Smaller projects get tighter maxOutputChars, smaller defaultMaxFiles, narrower gapThreshold, and no meta-text overhead.

features.name: kindBonus per-kind scoring weights
features.counter_case: Cortex's entities are not typed by 'kind' today; the weights only apply if Cortex distinguishes classes/functions/routes in search results.
features.summary: function/method=10, interface=9, route=9, class=8, type_alias=6, struct=6, component=8, enum=5, property/field=3, import/export=1, parameter=0.

features.name: WSL2 /mnt drive watch policy (detectWsl + WatchProbe testability)
features.counter_case: Cortex's watcher isn't built yet (Phase 0.8 / 5.6 planned); adding WSL detection before the watcher exists is premature.
features.summary: CODEGRAPH_NO_WATCH=1 always off, CODEGRAPH_FORCE_WATCH=1 always on, otherwise disables on WSL2+/mnt/ (recursive fs.watch too slow). Returns human-readable reason string.

features.name: BFS structural edge priority sort (contains > calls > other)
features.counter_case: Cortex's graph traversal (Phase 9 impact analysis) may use a different priority model; imposing codegraph's order could change blast-radius calculation results.
features.summary: Before fanning out from a node, sorts adjacent edges: contains=0, calls=1, other=2. Internal structure is discovered before external references (e.g. component usages in templates).

features.name: Agent evaluation framework (recall/MRR, real-world corpus.json)
features.counter_case: Cortex's Phase 0.11 is about token-cost benchmarks, not search-quality metrics; recall/MRR are search quality measures that require a different evaluation harness.
features.summary: PASS_THRESHOLD=0.5, recall = found/expected, MRR = 1/firstRank. Real-world corpus spans 5 languages × S/M/L sizes. Runs via 'npm run eval' against indexed repos.

features.name: Rust crate/super/self path prefix stripping for symbol resolution
features.counter_case: Cortex doesn't parse Rust yet; this is only relevant after Phase 0.13 adds Rust extraction.
features.summary: RUST_PATH_PREFIXES = {crate, super, self}. Stripping these before file-path matching makes 'crate::configurator::run' resolve identically to 'configurator::run'.

features.name: CHANGELOG-driven release notes extraction script
features.counter_case: Cortex's Phase 12.11 is about generating changelogs, not extracting them; this script is for release automation, not architectural changelog generation.
features.summary: Extracts specific version section from CHANGELOG.md (or [Unreleased] fallback) for GitHub Release notes. Used in release.yml workflow.

features.name: Multi-agent installer architecture (one-file-per-target, detectAll with auto-fallback)
features.counter_case: Cortex's Phase 0.15 has a different multi-target design (skill + MCP + auto-config writer); adopting codegraph's target interface would require adapting to Cortex's distribution model.
features.summary: AgentTarget interface: id, detect(), write(), remove(). resolveTargetFlag('auto') detects installed agents, falls back to claude. One new target = 1 file + 1 registry.ts entry.

features.name: Self-contained bundled distribution (vendored Node per platform)
features.counter_case: Cortex's Phase 0.17 plans a standalone binary; codegraph's approach bundles Node itself (not compile to binary), which is a different distribution model with different tradeoffs.
features.summary: Vendored Node 24 per platform (darwin-arm64/x64, linux-x64/arm64, win32-x64/arm64). Zero native addons. Thin npm shim + optionalDependencies per platform. Cross-builds on one Linux runner.

features.name: codegraph status CLI (basic index stats, backend info)
features.steel_man: codegraph status is simple and works today; cortex doctor is planned and may be over-engineered with cycle detection.
features.summary: Reports node/edge/file counts, SQLite backend (native vs WASM), and journal mode. Simpler than planned Phase 0.7 but functional.

features.name: FTS5 as search backend (keyword BM25 scoring)
features.steel_man: codegraph's FTS5 implementation is working today on real codebases; Cortex's planned FTS5+RRF pipeline may be over-complicated for the knowledge-base search use case.
features.summary: SQLite FTS5 with BM25 via fts5(content='nodes', content_rowid='rowid'). Cortex plans the same but also adds RRF, Levenshtein, and MMR layers.

features.name: Synchronous execSync in PreToolUse hooks (Cortex flaw #66)
features.why_target_chose: Cortex's inject-knowledge.js used execSync because it predates the async-background pattern; synchronous shell-out was the simplest way to guarantee output arrives before the tool result.
features.flaws_md_addition:
### Flaw #118 — Synchronous shell-out in PreToolUse hooks
**Severity**: 3
**Description**: Using execSync in PreToolUse hooks blocks the event loop for every Read/Grep tool call. The correct pattern (per codegraph's git-hooks.ts:73) is async background: `( codegraph sync >/dev/null 2>&1 & ) >/dev/null 2>&1`. Blocking hooks add 100-500ms latency on every native tool call and make the IDE feel sluggish.
**Source-of-lesson**: codegraph/src/sync/git-hooks.ts:73-80
features.summary: Anti-pattern: synchronous exec in hooks blocks event loop. codegraph's correct async alternative: `( cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 & ) >/dev/null 2>&1`.

features.name: Should Cortex adopt codegraph as its underlying AST indexer?
features.summary: codegraph already depends on projectcortex (file:../LLM-Cortex). Could Cortex delegate AST extraction to codegraph, or is the dependency direction wrong?
alternatives: A: Cortex builds its own tree-sitter layer (Phase 0.13) independently
B: Cortex delegates all AST extraction to codegraph and drops Phase 0.13
C: Optional bridge — Cortex uses codegraph when present, falls back to its own extractors

features.name: Should Cortex expose field-qualified search syntax?
features.summary: kind:function path:src/api is powerful but adds query complexity. Should cortex_find accept structured filters or stay free-text-only?
alternatives: B: Separate filter params on the MCP tool (no new syntax)
C: Keep free-text only (simpler mental model)

features.name: Should Cortex's output budgeting be project-size-adaptive or fixed?
features.summary: codegraph scales 8 output parameters across 4 file-count tiers. Is file-count the right signal for Cortex (which uses entity/token counts, not file counts)?
alternatives: A: Same 4-tier file-count approach as codegraph
B: Token-budget-driven (more aligned with Cortex's existing budget system)

features.name: Impact analysis / blast-radius traversal
features.summary: codegraph has codegraph_impact; Cortex has impact_analysis (Phase 6, done).

features.name: Context building for AI consumption
features.summary: codegraph has build_context / ContextBuilder; Cortex has build_context_pack (Phase 13, done).

features.name: Basic MCP server with multiple tools
features.summary: Both expose an MCP server. Cortex Phase 4 done.

features.name: Graph traversal (BFS/DFS)
features.summary: Cortex has impact traversal; codegraph has full BFS/DFS with TraversalOptions.
